title: Cheaper-config quality gates and eval scenarios
content:
Purpose:

This is a working draft that proposes a lightweight, reproducible gating framework for promoting cheaper serving configurations (quantized models, smaller variants, micro-batching, cache policies) into production without measurable customer-facing quality regressions. The goal is to convert the cost/perf tradeoffs in our modeling spreadsheets into operational decision rules used by rollouts (canary, A/B, auto-fallback).

Background / motivation:
- Customers and internal SREs want predictable unit economics; Optimize team owns recommendations but we need a deterministic way to say when a cheaper config is acceptable.
- Previous ad-hoc experiments showed up to 3x cost reduction for low-criticality workloads with minimal quality delta on average, but edge-case regressions occurred in ~0.7% of prompts.
- Need an automated gate that is: (a) fast to compute on each candidate, (b) aligned with per-workload risk tolerance, (c) easy to inspect or roll back.

Definitions and primitives:
- Baseline: current production config for a route (model variant + quantization + batching + cache configuration).
- Candidate: cheaper config being evaluated (examples: fp16->int8, base->small model, batchsize 1->4).
- Eval set: route-specific prompt suite (stratified across critical, common, and long-tail prompts). Each eval set has explicit slices flagged as "safety/critical" (must not regress).
- Quality metric(s): numeric scores computed by our eval harness. Primary metrics by workload type: 
  * RAG / LLM answers: instruction-following score (0-100), semantic similarity (embedding cosine) to reference, factuality check pass rate.
  * Classification: accuracy / macro-F1.
  * Extraction: token-level F1.
  * Embeddings: average cosine with baseline / downstream task delta.
- Cost metric: expected per-1K-token USD (or normalized cost multiplier). Latency SLO impact: p50/p95/p99 additional ms.

Proposed gating rules (high-level):
1) Per-workload risk profile: assign each route to a risk tier: low / medium / high. Default map in spreadsheet.
2) Global acceptance criteria for candidate config (must pass all):
   a) Overall eval-score delta <= tier-specific threshold (relative to baseline). Example thresholds: low: <= 6% drop, medium: <= 3% drop, high: <= 1% drop.
   b) No failing regressions on any "safety/critical" slice (strict equality/no drop).
   c) Embedding-semantic shift <= 0.02 cosine for retrieval-heavy routes.
   d) Latency p99 increase <= tier-specific SLO (default +50ms for low, +25ms for medium, +10ms for high).
   e) Expected cost improvement >= minimal improvement threshold (default 12% for low-risk, 6% for medium, 3% for high).
3) Canary rollout policy for accepted candidates:
   - Start at 1% traffic for 24 hours with monitoring hooks (error rate, latency, per-request quality delta sampled).
   - If no alerts and sampled evals match off-line predictions, increase to 10% for 48 hours, then 50% for 72 hours before full promotion.
4) Auto-fallback triggers: immediate rollback if: error rate > baseline + 0.5% absolute, or 7-day sampled eval drift > threshold, or customer complaint flags (internal signal).

Evaluation methodology (how to measure):
- Each candidate must be run through the standard "optimize/eval-harness" (linked) with: 
  * N=2k stratified prompts as default per-route eval set. Smaller routes (<=200 users/day) can use N=500 with higher conservatism.
  * 3 random seeds / temperature sweeps for generative outputs to capture variability.
  * Produce the following outputs: per-prompt baseline score, per-prompt candidate score, delta, slice-level aggregated metrics, and distribution of deltas.
- Compute: mean delta, 90th-percentile negative delta, count of prompts with delta > tier-violation.
- Bootstrapped confidence intervals recommended for small eval sets.

Spreadsheet model (columns and recommended schema):
- config_id (string), model_variant (string), quant_mode (string), batch_size (int), cache_policy (string), expected_cost_multiplier (float expressed as pct), run_date, eval_set_id, baseline_score, candidate_score, mean_delta_pct, p90_negative_delta_pct, critical_slice_failures (int), expected_p99_latency_delta_ms, decision (approve/reject/needs-more-data), notes.
- We recommend adding: risk_tier, required_min_cost_win_pct.
- Example row (human-readable): "c_032 | llama-2-13b -> quant8 | batch4 | prefix-kv-cache-on | -36% cost | baseline 87.2 -> candidate 84.1 | mean -3.6% | p90 -8.1% | critical_fail 0 | +6ms p99 | approve (low-risk)"

Scenario examples (short):
- Scenario A (low-risk chat bot): baseline 13B fp16 -> candidate 13B int8; expected -28% cost, mean quality -2.8% (passes low-risk gate), p99 +9ms (acceptable), promote with 1% canary.
- Scenario B (high-risk billing QA): baseline 70B -> candidate 70B q4_0; mean quality -1.8% (fails high-tier 1% threshold), reject and run smaller candidate search (e.g., maintain model but tune batching/CPU placement instead).
- Scenario C (embeddings for semantic search): baseline ada-like -> candidate ada-quant; embedding cosine drop 0.015 (acceptable if retrieval pipeline can tolerate), cost -40% => approve for low/medium; run A/B downstream retrieval metric check.

Operational notes and gotchas (lessons from prior experiments):
- Aggregate means can hide long-tail regressions: always check p90/p95 negative delta slices.
- Some prompts are brittle to quantization (long code completions, precise numeric outputs). Maintain a curated "do-not-quantize" set for routes needing exactness.
- Batching sometimes improves cost but increases tail latency: watch p99.
- When using smaller eval sets, add a conservative buffer to thresholds (e.g., halved acceptable delta).

Ownership and playbook steps for a candidate: 
1) Engineer or SRE opens an "optimize candidate" spreadsheet row and links PR/Jira.
2) Run eval-harness and attach artifacts to the row.
3) Product/Optimize reviewer reviews deltas and assigns risk_tier if not set.
4) If gates pass, schedule canary with rollout playbook and monitor metrics.
5) Record outcome and update the config catalog.

Next actions / open questions (TODOs):
- Define exact per-workload default thresholds (proposal above; need alignment from PMs/prod-eng).
- Add a sampling pipeline to automatically run candidate evals nightly for queued candidates.
- Build dashboard tile in Console to show candidate vs baseline cost/quality scatter and failed prompts list.
- Small pilot: pick 4 low-risk routes next quarter and try 3 candidate configs each; measure cost delta and customer-visible errors.

Notes-to-self / quick checklist: 
- [ ] Add template row in Google Sheet with example values.
- [ ] Add a short doc for Solutions Eng on how to interpret eval deltas.
- [ ] Get sign-off from legal on any changes that touch customer-facing determinism for regulated customers.
